skill.name: scaffold-exercises
skill.description: Create course exercise folders with sections, exercise variants, readme stubs, lint checks, and git-friendly move guidance.
skill.summary: Scaffold structured course exercises with problem, solution, and explainer folders that pass project lint rules.

content.value_statement: Course exercise setup can be slow and inconsistent across sections. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code create lint-ready exercise folders with clear variants and readme stubs.
actual_capabilities: Creates numbered section and exercise directory structures under an exercises folder.
Uses problem, solution, and explainer variants based on the course plan.
Generates minimal readme stubs with titles and descriptions for each variant.
Runs the project lint command to validate scaffolded exercise structure.
Guides git-friendly exercise renaming with git mv when numbering changes.
limitations: Requires an existing project that uses the documented exercises folder convention.
Does not design full lesson content beyond minimal starter readme text.
Depends on the project linter being available in the local environment.
May need user review for final exercise titles, ordering, and learning goals.

use_cases.title: Create a new course section
use_cases.description: Turn a planned section outline into numbered exercise folders with explainer, problem, and solution variants.

use_cases.title: Stub exercises before writing content
use_cases.description: Prepare a clean directory skeleton so writers can fill in examples, instructions, and reference solutions later.

use_cases.title: Renumber existing exercises
use_cases.description: Move exercises into a new order while preserving git history and rerunning lint checks after changes.

prompt_templates.title: Scaffold a simple section
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request with one section and default explainer folders.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use scaffold-exercises to create a new section called Retrieval Basics with three explainer exercises: Intro, Keyword Search, and Evaluation.

prompt_templates.title: Create mixed exercise variants
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request with problem and solution folders.
prompt_templates.prompt: Scaffold section 04, Tool Calling. Add 04.01 Tool Schemas as an explainer, and 04.02 Build a Tool with explainer, problem, and solution variants.

prompt_templates.title: Apply a detailed course plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request using a supplied outline.
prompt_templates.prompt: Read this course plan and scaffold every listed exercise. Use explainer-only folders unless the plan explicitly asks for problem and solution variants.

prompt_templates.title: Renumber and validate exercises
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced maintenance request after a course reorder.
prompt_templates.prompt: Renumber the exercises in section 03 so the evaluation exercise comes before deployment. Use git mv, update folder names, and run the linter.

output_examples.input: Scaffold a Memory Skill Building section with introduction, short-term memory, and long-term memory exercises.
output: Creates a numbered Memory Skill Building section folder.
Adds explainer folders for introduction and long-term memory.
Adds explainer, problem, and solution folders for short-term memory when requested.
Creates readme stubs and reports lint results.

output_examples.input: Move an exercise later in the section while keeping history.
output_examples.output: Renames the exercise folder with git-friendly move steps, keeps numbering consistent, and reruns the course linter.

best_practices: Provide section numbers, exercise numbers, and exact variant types when possible.
Review generated readme titles before adding full teaching content.
Run the linter after scaffolding or moving exercises.
anti_patterns: Do not use it for projects without the expected exercises directory convention.
Do not treat readme stubs as finished instructional content.
Do not bypass lint failures after creating or moving exercise folders.

faq.question: What does this skill create?
faq.answer: It creates exercise folders, variant subfolders, and minimal readme stubs that follow the project convention.

faq.question: Does it write complete lessons?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on structure and starter readme files, not full teaching material.

faq.question: Which exercise variants are supported?
faq.answer: It supports problem, solution, and explainer folders, including mixed variants for one exercise.

faq.question: Can it rename existing exercises?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides guidance to use git mv so file history is preserved during renumbering.

faq.question: Does it require local commands?
faq.answer: Yes. It expects local filesystem changes and the project lint command to validate the result.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. It is suitable for Claude Code when working inside a repository that matches the exercise structure.
